name: Burpee Box Jump
description: The burpee box jump combines the full-body conditioning demand of a burpee with the explosive vertical jump mechanics of a box jump, requiring the athlete to perform a burpee on the floor in front of a plyo box and then immediately jump onto the box. It is one of the most metabolically demanding plyometric exercises, training both the aerobic and anaerobic energy systems while developing lower body explosive power under fatigued conditions — closely mimicking the demands of competitive functional fitness.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a plyo box at a distance of roughly one step away.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a sturdy plyo box of appropriate height (20–24 inches for most athletes). Ensure the box does not slide.
steps: Step 1: Perform a full burpee — squat down, kick feet back to plank, do a push-up, return feet to squat.
Step 2: From the squat position, explosively jump forward and upward onto the plyo box.
Step 3: Land on the box with both feet, absorbing through the hips and knees.
Step 4: Stand tall on the box, then step down (not jump down) to the starting position.
Step 5: Immediately begin the next burpee.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously. Exhale on the push-up press and on the box jump.
common_mistakes: Jumping down from the box — step down to protect the Achilles and knees on fatigued landings
Rushing the burpee so the push-up is sloppy
Undershooting the box jump when fatigued — reduce box height before reducing effort
safety_considerations: Very high demand — only for well-conditioned athletes with established burpee and box jump proficiency.
Always step down from the box, never jump down when fatigued.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up depth. Full extension on box jump. Full standing on the box.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Performed for reps (5–10) or time (20–40 second efforts). Full recovery between sets.
coaching_cues: Hips fully open at the top of the jump
